problem_statement: A projectile of mass $m = 0.50\text{ kg}$ is fired from the origin $O$ on flat ground with initial speed $v_0 = 20.0\text{ m/s}$ at an angle $\theta = 60.0^\circ$ above the horizontal. Taking $g = 10.0\text{ m/s}^2$ downward along the $-y$ axis, find: (a) the angular momentum vector $\vec{L}_O$ of the projectile about the launch point $O$ at the instant it reaches the peak of its trajectory, and (b) the angular momentum vector $\vec{L}_O$ just before landing back on the ground.
target_quantity: Angular momentum vector L_O at peak and at landing
governing_principles: Definition of particle angular momentum: L_O = r x p = m (r x v)
Torque-angular momentum relation: tau_O = dL_O / dt => L_O(t) = int_0^t tau_O(t') dt'
solution_strategy: Method 1: Direct definition L_O = r x p. At peak, find coordinates (x_h, y_h) and velocity v_h. At landing, find (R, 0) and v_land. Method 2: Torque integration tau_O = r x (-m g j) = -m g x(t) k = -m g v_0 cos(theta) t k => L_O(t) = -1/2 m g v_0 cos(theta) t^2 k.

ordered_steps.equation: t_{\text{peak}} = \frac{v_0 \sin\theta}{g}, \quad x_{\text{peak}} = v_0 \cos\theta \, t_{\text{peak}}, \quad y_{\text{peak}} = H = \frac{v_0^2 \sin^2\theta}{2g}, \quad \vec{v}_{\text{peak}} = v_0 \cos\theta \, \hat{i}
ordered_steps.substitution: t_{\text{peak}} = \frac{20.0 \sin 60^\circ}{10.0} = \sqrt{3}\text{ s} \approx 1.732\text{ s}, \quad x_{\text{peak}} = 10.0\sqrt{3}\text{ m}, \quad y_{\text{peak}} = \frac{400(3/4)}{20} = 15.0\text{ m}, \quad \vec{v} = 10.0 \, \hat{i}\text{ m/s}
ordered_steps.intermediate_result: r_peak = 10 sqrt(3) i + 15.0 j, v_peak = 10.0 i

ordered_steps.principle_applied: Vector cross product definition at apex
Kinematics and torque integration to landing
ordered_steps.equation: T_{\text{flight}} = 2 t_{\text{peak}} = 2\sqrt{3}\text{ s}, \quad \vec{L}_O(t) = -\frac{1}{2} m g v_0 \cos\theta \, t^2 \, \hat{k}

sanity_checks: Quadratic scaling: Because torque is tau = -m g v_0 cos(theta) t, angular momentum scales quadratically as t^2. Since T_flight = 2 t_peak, L_land / L_peak = (2)^2 = 4. Indeed, -300.0 / -75.0 = 4.00! Exact agreement.

Cross product check at landing: r_land = R i, v_land = v_0x i - v_0y j. L_land = R i x m(v_0x i - v_0y j) = -m R v_0y k. Here R = v_0^2 sin(2 theta)/g = 400(sqrt(3)/2)/10 = 20 sqrt(3) m. L_land = -0.50 (20 sqrt(3))(10 sqrt(3)) k = -0.50(600) k = -300.0 k. Dual derivation confirms result bit-for-bit.
alternate_methods: Time integral of torque tau(t) = r(t) x F_g.
